teaser.slogan: Dive into the world of Logic Circuits for free!
teaser.description:
Build your own circuits, from a single gate to a complete sequential design. Plus exercises, explanations and learning material - all in the same browser.

No account, no install. Draw a circuit, start the simulation, current flows.

demo.slogan: Building your very first circuit it's easy as 1..2..3
demo.description1: Design circuits quickly and easily with a modern and intuitive user interface with drag-and-drop, copy/paste, zoom and more.
demo.description2: With Electra.Academy, you can edit and run your digital circuit simulation designs online within your browser and trigger any physical device.

slidedeck1.slogan: Visual connect, control, and learn digital electronics
slidedeck1.description:
Circuits make sense once you build them.
With Electra.Simulator you drag gates onto the canvas, wire them up and watch the current flow - no sign-up, straight in the browser.

And when something does not work, you see why. What you build, someone else can open, understand and build on.

slidedeck2.slogan: Designed to be very easy to use in classes
slidedeck2.description:
The best exercise is the one that gets passed on.
With Electra.Author you write learning material: circuits, tables, cloze texts, flashcards and formulas, all in the same editor.

A good exercise helps one class. Shared, it helps many.

slidedeck3.description:
Missing a part? Then build it.
With Electra.Designer you draw your own components and bring them to life with a few lines of JavaScript.

After that it sits in the simulator - for you, and for everyone who can use it.

slidedeck4.slogan: Welcome in the Universe of Electra Academy

footer.tagline: Electra.Academy is a free platform for digital circuit design. Build, simulate and understand - in the browser, nothing to install. Free for schools.

section02.body:

Should we ever use non-essential cookies - for statistics or advertising, say - we will ask for your consent first and update this page.

section04.header: How to delete or block cookies
section04.body: You can view, delete or block cookies and local storage at any time in your browser settings. If you block the strictly necessary entries, sign-in and remembering your language may stop working.

section01.body: The controller for the processing described here is the provider named in the imprint, where you will also find the full contact details.

section02.body:
Without signing in, we store no personal data about you. You can read the start page, the legal texts and use the simulator without us knowing who you are.

Once you sign in, we store your e-mail address. It is the key that ties together:
  • which circuits and documents belong to you
  • which groups or classes you belong to, and what that gives you access to
The e-mail address is stored in clear text, not encrypted or obscured. That is a deliberate choice: teachers assemble groups by e-mail address, so obscuring it would only provide apparent security.

We do not evaluate what you look at, how long you stay or where you came from. There is no profiling and no disclosure for advertising purposes.

section03.body:
Signing in works via Google Single Sign-On. You need a Google account for it - there is no separate password with us.

When Google is involved at all: Google's sign-in code is loaded only inside the applications (simulator, author, designer). On the start page and on these information pages nothing is loaded from Google - you can read them in full without any connection to Google being made.

What Google passes to us when you sign in: e-mail address, display name, given and family name, and the address of your profile picture. Of these we permanently store only the e-mail address (see above); name and picture are held for the duration of your session only, to show you in the interface.

Transfer to the USA: Google is a US company. Signing in transfers data to the United States, a country outside the EU. The legal basis is your consent under Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR - you give it by choosing to sign in. If you would rather not, use the platform without signing in.

Minors: Art. 8 GDPR governs consent by minors; in Germany, consent by a parent or guardian is required for children under 16. Before using the platform with sign-in, schools should check whether they may require learners to hold an account with a commercial provider - several federal states restrict this.

section04.body: Technical log data is produced when the site is accessed, as with any web server. These logs are anonymous: they contain no e-mail addresses and are not evaluated to trace the behaviour of individuals. They are not combined with your account and no usage profiles are created.

section05.body:
We process personal data only where there is a legal basis for it:
  • Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract) for everything belonging to signed-in operation - your account, your saved circuits and documents, and group membership.
  • Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR (consent) for signing in via Google and the transfer to the USA that comes with it. You give it by choosing to sign in, and may withdraw it at any time by no longer signing in or having your account deleted.
  • Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interests) for the technical log data needed for secure and trouble-free operation.
For minors, Art. 8 GDPR applies in addition.

section06.body:
The application and all stored content are hosted on servers in Europe and are therefore subject to the GDPR.

There is one exception: signing in via Google. That transfers data to a US company and thus to a third country - see the section on signing in with Google for details. If you use the platform without signing in, your data does not leave the European legal area.

section07.body:
Under the GDPR you have the following rights:
  • Access (Art. 15) to the data we process about you
  • Rectification of inaccurate data (Art. 16)
  • Erasure (Art. 17)
  • Restriction of processing (Art. 18)
  • Data portability (Art. 20)
  • Objection to processing (Art. 21)
  • Withdrawal of consent given (Art. 7(3)), effective for the future
An informal e-mail to the address given in the imprint is enough for any of these.

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR), usually the authority of your federal state or your habitual residence.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: This page is quickly explained, because Electra.Academy is not software you buy and not a service that locks you in. It is an open place to build, understand and pass on. What follows mainly describes how that place works - and what you get out of joining in.

section01.header: An open platform - and what that means
section01.body:
The whole point of this platform is sharing knowledge. A circuit somebody else can open, understand and build on is worth more than one sitting in a drawer.

So everything here is built to be passed on. What you save can be shared - by you, and by everyone you work with in a group. There is no way to lock an individual item away, and we do not want one: a platform where every item has to be released first would be the opposite of what it was built for.

In practice that means: treat everything you put here as something that can find its way out. We cannot and do not promise that anything stays private.

Turn it around and it becomes the upside: you get to draw on everything others have shared. That is exactly the idea.

section02.body:
Because everything can be shared, the reverse holds: what has to stay confidential does not belong here.

That applies above all to personal data. Names, contact details, grades, assessments and the like have no place in titles, labels and texts - neither your own nor anyone else's. Name a task after the subject rather than a person: "Task 3, gate logic" instead of someone's name.

Content that infringes the rights of others does not belong here either: third-party material without permission, anything abusive or unlawful.

Anyone misusing the platform to harm others or disrupt its operation can be excluded from using it.

section03.body:
Electra.Academy is free and run by a single person. That leads to an honest statement: there is no guarantee of availability, maintenance windows or response times. There can be outages, and operation may change.

If you want to be safe - and for anything you rely on you should be: keep copies of your work. The platform is open source, and you can run it yourself if it comes to that. This is exactly why the code is public.

No liability is accepted for damage arising from use, as far as the law permits. Liability for intent and gross negligence, and for injury to life, body or health, is unaffected.

section04.body:
The best thing that can happen to this platform is someone sharing a good exercise, or building a circuit so clearly that the next person understands it instantly.

If something is missing, something gets in the way, or you have an idea: the ways to reach us are in the footer of this page. The source is open, feedback is welcome, and contributions are too.

about.title: About me
about.intro:
Electra.Academy is a workshop for digital circuits in your browser. Drag gates onto the canvas, wire them up, and watch what happens - no setup, no installation, no waiting for the lab to be free.

The difference to a picture in a textbook: here the circuit is alive. Flip a switch and you can see the current run through the wires. Build something wrong and you see why it does not work. That is the moment understanding happens - not while memorising a truth table.

section01.body:
A single developer, by conviction - and has been since university.

Back then I got hooked on the question of how to not merely draw a circuit but bring it to life. That question never let go. Out of it grew first draw2d.js, an open source library for drawing and connecting diagrams in the browser that is used in projects around the world today - and then Electra.Academy, built right on top of it. What you drag across the canvas here is that same engine.

Both grew over years of evenings and weekends, with no company behind it, no investor, no marketing budget. The motivation is simple: digital electronics makes sense once you are allowed to touch it. Most people meet it as an abstract collection of formulas and give up before the good part starts. It does not have to be that way.

That is why there is no tracking, no advertising and no paywall. Not as a marketing promise - but because that is what a tool for schools should look like.

section02.header: Open source, and we mean it
section02.body:
All source code is public on GitHub under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Free to use for schools, educational institutions and non-profit groups.

Open source here also means you can check what happens. No hidden scripts, no analytics in the background, no service quietly collecting data. If you prefer, run the platform on your own school server - the code belongs to everyone.

And because one person cannot see everything: feedback from real lessons is the most valuable thing this project can get. What is missing, what gets in the way, what confuses students - please write. The ways to reach us are in the footer of this page.
